::: {#sol-scale-images}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
largest = images.float().amax(dim=(1, 2))
try:
    images.float() / largest
except RuntimeError as err:
    print(textwrap.fill(str(err), 60))

largest = images.float().amax(dim=(1, 2), keepdim=True)
scaled = images.float() / largest
all_ones = bool((scaled.amax(dim=(1, 2)) == 1).all())
print(largest.shape, scaled.shape, all_ones)
```

`.amax(dim=(1, 2))` takes the largest pixel over each image's rows and columns,
giving one number per image, a [tensor](#def-tensor) of [shape](#def-shape) (`r py$n_images`,).
Dividing by it fails.
By @def-broadcasting, the last dimensions line up first,
and they are 8 and `r py$n_images`, which differ with neither equal to 1.
`keepdim=True` keeps the two dimensions it reduced, with size 1,
so the largest pixels have shape (`r py$n_images`, 1, 1),
which broadcasts against (`r py$n_images`, 8, 8) as in @exm-broadcasting.
`r if (py$all_ones) "Every" else "Not every"` scaled image has 1 as its largest pixel.

:::
